mainTopic: The end of the story of אחר, whether one may learn תורה from a flawed teacher, and why some great scholars fell while רבי עקיבא came out safely
overview: The amud finishes the story of אחר (אלישע בן אבויה). רבי מאיר brings him to thirteen בתי כנסת, and each child quotes a harsh פסוק about the wicked. The last child's stutter makes the פסוק sound like it names אלישע himself. After אחר dies, רבי מאיר arranges for him to be judged so he can reach עולם הבא, and רבי יוחנן later gets him released. When אחר's daughter asks רבי for food, a fire from heaven shows that his תורה still deserves honor. The גמרא then asks how רבי מאיר could learn from אחר at all, and answers that an adult may take the good and throw away the bad, while a child may not. אליהו reports that Heaven agrees with רבי מאיר. שמואל explains that great scholars like דואג and אחיתופל fell only because of a flaw in their hearts, and the גמרא shows the same flaw in אחר. The amud ends by returning to the four in the פרדס: רבי עקיבא came out safely because ה׳ protected him.

steps.title: A child recites a harsh verse
steps.stepSummary: אחר asks a child for the פסוק he learned, and the child quotes a rebuke from ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to a child: Tell me your verse. The child said: 'And you, ruined one, what are you doing, dressing in scarlet, wearing gold jewelry, painting your eyes? You make yourself pretty for nothing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story is already in progress: אחר is asking a schoolchild which פסוק he learned, treating the answer like a sign from Heaven. The child answers with a פסוק saying that dressing up is useless for someone who is ruined.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Asking a child for his פסוק was an accepted way of looking for a hint about one's own situation. The answer suggests that outside good things cannot fix a ruined inner state, which hints that אחר cannot fix himself.

keyTerms.meaning: A young child, here a schoolchild
Recite your verse to me (tell me the פסוק you learned today)

phrases.english: [He said] to a child: Recite your verse to me.
phrases.notes: The speaker is אחר, checking which פסוק the kids learned that day.

phrases.english: He said to him: "And you, ruined one, what are you doing,
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 4:30

phrases.english: that you dress in scarlet,
that you put on golden jewelry,
that you widen your eyes with paint?
For nothing you make yourself beautiful, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of אחר from the earlier part of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child's פסוק hints that outward efforts are useless for one who is ruined

steps.title: Thirteen synagogues, the same kind of answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר takes אחר to more and more בתי כנסת, thirteen in all, and every child quotes a similar harsh פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: He brought him to another synagogue, until he had brought him into thirteen synagogues, and all of them recited verses like this one to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story repeats the test again and again. Every single child gives a פסוק that sounds just as hopeless for the wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The repetition makes the message stronger: this is not one unlucky answer but a steady pattern. Thirteen signs in a row point the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: In the same way, something similar

phrases.english: He brought him into another synagogue,
until he had brought him into thirteen synagogues,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלְּהוּ פְּסַקוּ לֵיהּ כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא.
phrases.english: and all of them recited to him [verses] like this one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the test of step 1 many more times
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every child gave a similarly harsh פסוק

steps.title: The last child's verse about the wicked
steps.stepSummary: In the last בית כנסת the child quotes the פסוק from תהלים: 'To the wicked God says: what right do you have to recite My laws?'
steps.simpleTranslation: At the last one, he said to him: Tell me your verse. He said: 'And to the wicked one God says: What right do you have to speak of My laws?'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last and sharpest answer. The פסוק says a wicked person has no right to talk about Torah, which hits אחר directly, since he was a great Torah scholar who sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier answers spoke about the wicked in general. This one is about a wicked person who teaches Torah, which describes אחר exactly.

phrases.aramaic: לְבָתְרָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּסוֹק לִי פְּסוּקָךְ.
phrases.english: At the last one, he said to him: Recite your verse to me.
He said to him: "And to the wicked one God says:
phrases.notes: תהלים 50:16

phrases.english: What right do you have to recite My laws, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final and most pointed answer in the series
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last פסוק speaks of a wicked person who talks about Torah

steps.title: The stutter that made the verse sound like 'Elisha'
steps.stepSummary: The child stuttered, so 'ולרשע' (to the wicked one) sounded like 'ולאלישע' (to Elisha).
steps.simpleTranslation: That child stuttered, so it sounded as if he said: 'And to Elisha God says.'
steps.whatsHappening: Because of the child's speech problem, the word for 'the wicked one' came out sounding like אחר's own name, אלישע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the message is not only about him, it seems to call him by name. This leads straight into אחר's angry reaction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It sounded like, it was heard as

phrases.english: That child stuttered with his tongue,
so it sounded as though he said to him:
"And to Elisha God says,"
phrases.notes: Say 'וְלָרָשָׁע' and 'וְלֶאֱלִישָׁע' out loud. With a stutter they really do sound alike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the last פסוק seemed to name אחר personally
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק sounded as if it named אלישע

steps.title: Two versions of אחר's angry reaction
steps.stepSummary: One version: אחר had a knife and killed the child, sending the pieces to the thirteen בתי כנסת. Another version: he only said he would have done so if he had a knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say he had a knife with him, and he tore the child apart and sent him to the thirteen synagogues. Others say he only said: If I had a knife in my hand, I would have torn him apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two traditions about what אחר did after hearing his 'name' in the פסוק. In one he actually acted; in the other he only spoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions show how far אחר had fallen, since he wanted to hurt a child for a פסוק. The difference is whether he carried it out or only said it.
steps.confusionAlert: These are two different versions of the story, not two things that both happened. The second version means he never actually hurt the child.

phrases.english: Some say: He had a knife with him,
and he tore him apart and sent him to the thirteen synagogues.
And some say that he said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי הֲוַאי בִּידִי סַכִּינָא, הֲוָה קָרַעְנָא לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: If I had a knife in my hand, I would have torn him apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes אחר's reaction to the child's words
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two traditions: he killed the child, or he only threatened to

steps.title: Heaven's decision when אחר died
steps.stepSummary: When אחר died, it was decided he would not be judged, because he had learned Torah, and would not enter עולם הבא, because he sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: When אחר died, they said: He should not be judged, and he should not come to the World to Come. Not judged, because he was busy with Torah. Not brought to the World to Come, because he sinned.
steps.whatsHappening: The story jumps to אחר's death and the heavenly ruling about him. He is left in between: no punishment, but also no reward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His Torah learning protected him from punishment in גיהנם, but his sins kept him out of עולם הבא. This 'stuck in the middle' state sets up רבי מאיר's response.

keyTerms.meaning: He passed away (literally: his soul rested)

phrases.english: When Acher passed away, they said:
phrases.notes: 'They' means the heavenly court that decides his fate.

phrases.english: He should not be judged,
and he should not come to the World to Come.

phrases.aramaic: לָא מֵידָן לִידַיְּינֵיהּ — מִשּׁוּם דַּעֲסַק בְּאוֹרָיְיתָא,
phrases.english: Not judged, because he was busy with Torah;

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא לְעָלְמָא דְּאָתֵי לֵיתֵי — מִשּׁוּם דַּחֲטָא.
phrases.english: and not brought to the World to Come, because he sinned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from אחר's life to what happened after his death
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אחר is neither judged nor admitted to עולם הבא

steps.title: רבי מאיר: better he be judged and then enter עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says it is better for אחר to be punished and then enter עולם הבא, and says that after his own death he will cause smoke to rise from אחר's grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: It is better that he be judged and then come to the World to Come. When I die, I will make smoke rise from his grave.
steps.whatsHappening: אחר's student, רבי מאיר, does not accept the in-between ruling. He plans to get his teacher judged so that afterward he can reach עולם הבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being punished in גיהנם is painful but it cleans a person, and then he can enter עולם הבא. Smoke from the grave would be the sign that the judgment had started.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said:
It is better that he be judged and come to the World to Come.
When I die, I will make smoke rise from his grave.
phrases.notes: The smoke is a sign that he is being judged in גיהנם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the heavenly decision with a better plan
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judgment followed by עולם הבא is better than being stuck in between

steps.title: Smoke rises from אחר's grave
steps.stepSummary: When רבי מאיר died, smoke rose from אחר's grave, so רבי מאיר's plan worked.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי מאיר died, smoke rose from אחר's grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The story confirms that רבי מאיר got what he asked for. אחר's judgment began.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows a student's merit affecting his teacher's fate. But the job is only half done, since אחר is now being judged and is not yet in עולם הבא.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Meir passed away,
smoke rose from Acher's grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי מאיר's plan coming true

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: is burning your teacher really a great deed?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן questions רבי מאיר's approach: a student should save his teacher completely. If we hold his hand, no one can take him away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Is it a great deed to burn your teacher? There was one among us, and we can't save him? If we hold him by the hand, who can take him away from us? Who?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges רבי מאיר's solution. He thinks it is not enough to get אחר punished; the scholars should save him outright.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר chose judgment as the way to reach עולם הבא. רבי יוחנן argues that one of our own scholars should be protected from suffering altogether, and that our hold on him is strong enough to do it.

keyTerms.meaning: If we hold him by the hand

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Is it a great deed to burn one's teacher?
There was one among us,
and we can't save him?
If we hold him by the hand,
who will take him away from us? Who?
phrases.notes: The last word 'מִן' just repeats the question 'who?' for emphasis.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Criticizes רבי מאיר's solution
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's choice to have אחר judged in גיהנם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A student should rescue his teacher fully rather than arrange his punishment; our hold on him is strong enough to save him

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's plan: stop the smoke
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that when he dies he will put out the smoke from אחר's grave.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: When I die, I will put out the smoke from his grave.
steps.whatsHappening: After his challenge, רבי יוחנן gives his own plan, the reverse of רבי מאיר's. He will end אחר's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר's sign was smoke rising, which meant judgment. רבי יוחנן's sign will be smoke stopping, which means אחר is freed and brought into עולם הבא.

phrases.english: He said: When I die,
I will put out the smoke from his grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי יוחנן's criticism into an action plan
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן will end אחר's judgment

steps.title: The smoke stops
steps.stepSummary: When רבי יוחנן died, the smoke from אחר's grave stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יוחנן died, the smoke stopped rising from אחר's grave.
steps.whatsHappening: The story confirms that רבי יוחנן's plan worked too. אחר's punishment ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together with step 8, the full arc is complete: first רבי מאיר got אחר judged, then רבי יוחנן got him released into עולם הבא.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Yochanan passed away,
the smoke stopped from Acher's grave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבי יוחנן's plan coming true

steps.title: The eulogy: even the gatekeeper couldn't stop you
steps.stepSummary: A eulogizer at רבי יוחנן's funeral says that even the guard at the entrance could not stand in his way.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain eulogizer opened his eulogy about him: Even the guard of the gate could not stand before you, our teacher!
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with praise of רבי יוחנן. His merit was so great that even the guard of גיהנם's gate could not keep אחר in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eulogy explains the meaning of the stopped smoke: רבי יוחנן overpowered the guard who keeps people in גיהנם. It closes the story of אחר on a note of rescue.

keyTerms.meaning: The guard of the gate (here, of גיהנם)

steps.whatToRemember: אחר was first left in between, neither judged nor rewarded. רבי מאיר got him judged (smoke rose), and רבי יוחנן got him released into עולם הבא (smoke stopped). The lesson: Torah learning and the efforts of later scholars can still rescue someone who strayed.

phrases.english: A certain eulogizer opened about him:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ שׁוֹמֵר הַפֶּתַח לֹא עָמַד לְפָנֶיךָ, רַבֵּינוּ!
phrases.english: Even the guard of the gate could not stand before you, our teacher!
phrases.notes: The 'gate' is the entrance of גיהנם. Even its guard couldn't stop רבי יוחנן from freeing אחר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story by explaining the power behind the stopped smoke
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן's merit overcame the guard of גיהנם and brought אחר out

steps.title: The daughter of אחר asks רבי for support
steps.stepSummary: A woman comes to רבי asking for food, and when asked who she is, she says she is the daughter of אחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter of אחר came before רבי. She said to him: רבי, support me. He said to her: Whose daughter are you? She said to him: I am the daughter of אחר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about אחר's daughter coming to רבי for help. This sets up the next move, where רבי reacts to who she is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were about what happened to אחר after he died. Now we hear about someone he left behind in this world. Her saying who her father is creates the problem in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The daughter of אחר (אלישע בן אבויה)

phrases.aramaic: בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל אַחֵר אָתְיָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי,
phrases.english: The daughter of Acher came before Rebbi,
She said to him: Rebbi, support me.
He said to her: Whose daughter are you?

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל אַחֵר אֲנִי.
phrases.english: She said to him: I am the daughter of Acher.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל אַחֵר אָתְיָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about אחר after the stories about his grave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter of אחר asks רבי for support and tells him who she is.

steps.title: רבי is surprised that אחר has any children left
steps.stepSummary: רבי quotes a פסוק saying a wicked person has no children left, so how can אחר have a daughter?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: Is there still any of his children left in the world? But it is written: 'He shall have no son and no grandson among his people, and no one left in his home'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי challenges her: according to a פסוק, a wicked man like אחר should not have any children left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי sees אחר as the wicked man described in the פסוק in איוב. If the פסוק says such a person has no children left, then her being alive seems to go against it. In his eyes, she should not be getting help.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהּ: עֲדַיִין יֵשׁ מִזַּרְעוֹ בָּעוֹלָם?!
phrases.english: He said to her: Are there still any of his children in the world?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כְּתִיב: ״לֹא נִין לוֹ וְלֹא נֶכֶד בְּעַמּוֹ
phrases.english: But it is written: "He shall have no son and no grandson among his people,
and no one left in his home"!
phrases.notes: איוב 18:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to her saying she is אחר's daughter.
steps.kashyaTarget: That אחר still has a daughter alive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק says a wicked person has no children left, so a child of אחר seems to go against the פסוק.

steps.title: Remember his תורה, not his deeds, and a fire backs her up
steps.stepSummary: She tells רבי to think about her father's תורה rather than his sins, and a fire from heaven burns רבי's bench.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: Remember his תורה, and do not remember his deeds. Right away a fire came down and burned the bench of רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter answers רבי: judge her father by his תורה learning, not by his sins. A fire from heaven shows that she is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She does not deny that אחר sinned. She says his תורה still counts for something. The fire on רבי's bench shows that heaven agrees and is protecting the honor of אחר's תורה.

phrases.english: She said to him: Remember his Torah,
and do not remember his deeds.
Immediately a fire came down
and burned the bench of Rebbi.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי's objection to helping her.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the focus from the father's sins to his תורה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since אחר was wicked, his children deserve nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The merit of his תורה still stands, and heaven protects it.

steps.title: רבי's lesson: how much more for those who honor תורה
steps.stepSummary: רבי cries and learns a קל וחומר: if heaven protects the honor of someone who disgraced the תורה, it surely does so for those who honor it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי cried and said: If this is what happens for those who disgrace the תורה, then for those who bring honor to it, how much more so!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ends the story by crying and drawing a lesson from what just happened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחר disgraced the תורה, yet heaven still defended the honor of his learning. So רבי reasons with a קל וחומר: people who honor the תורה will surely be protected even more. The story ends on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who bring honor and praise (to the תורה)
How much more so (a קל וחומר)

steps.whatToRemember: Even the תורה of אחר was honored by heaven. That shows how much more those who honor תורה are protected.

phrases.english: Rebbi cried and said:
If for those who disgrace it, it is like this,
phrases.notes: "It" means the תורה. אחר is the one who disgraced it.

phrases.aramaic: לַמִּשְׁתַּבְּחִין בָּהּ — עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה!
phrases.english: then for those who bring it honor, how much more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the lesson from the fire in the previous step.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Heaven protects the honor of תורה, even when the person who learned it went bad, and surely for those who honor it.

steps.title: How could רבי מאיר learn תורה from אחר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר could learn from אחר, since רבי יוחנן teaches that you only learn תורה from a teacher who is like an angel.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר, how could he learn תורה from the mouth of אחר? But רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: What does the פסוק mean, 'For the lips of the כהן should keep knowledge, and they should seek תורה from his mouth, for he is an angel of ה׳ of hosts'? If the teacher is like an angel of ה׳, they should seek תורה from his mouth. If not, they should not seek תורה from his mouth!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a question: how was רבי מאיר allowed to learn תורה from אחר, who had become a sinner?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק in מלאכי as a rule: you may learn תורה only from a teacher who behaves like an angel. אחר clearly did not, so רבי מאיר seems to have broken this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: An angel of ה׳ of hosts

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הֵיכִי גְּמַר תּוֹרָה מִפּוּמֵּיהּ דְּאַחֵר?
phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir, how could he learn Torah from the mouth of Acher?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabba bar bar Chana say in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי שִׂפְתֵי כֹהֵן יִשְׁמְרוּ דַעַת
phrases.english: What is meant by what is written: "For the lips of the priest should keep knowledge,

phrases.aramaic: וְתוֹרָה יְבַקְשׁוּ מִפִּיהוּ כִּי מַלְאַךְ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת הוּא״.
phrases.english: and they should seek Torah from his mouth, for he is an angel of the Lord of hosts"?
phrases.notes: מלאכי 2:7

phrases.aramaic: אִם דּוֹמֶה הָרַב לְמַלְאַךְ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת —
phrases.english: If the teacher is like an angel of the Lord of hosts,
they should seek Torah from his mouth,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אַל יְבַקְּשׁוּ תּוֹרָה מִפִּיהוּ!
phrases.english: and if not, they should not seek Torah from his mouth!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר, הֵיכִי גְּמַר תּוֹרָה מִפּוּמֵּיהּ דְּאַחֵר? וְהָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the larger story of רבי מאיר and אחר and questions it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's learning תורה from אחר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's reading of the פסוק allows learning only from a teacher who is like an angel, and אחר was not.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: רבי מאיר relied on a פסוק in משלי
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that רבי מאיר used a פסוק saying to apply your heart to 'My knowledge', meaning ה׳'s truth, not the teacher's own ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: רבי מאיר found a פסוק and explained it: 'Incline your ear and listen to the words of the wise, and apply your heart to My knowledge.' It does not say 'to their knowledge', but 'to My knowledge'.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question by showing that רבי מאיר had his own פסוק that allowed him to learn from אחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says to listen to the wise but to set your heart on 'My knowledge', meaning ה׳'s. So you may listen to a flawed teacher, as long as you hold on only to what matches ה׳'s truth and not to the teacher's own ways.

keyTerms.meaning: He found a פסוק and explained it

steps.confusionAlert: At this point ריש לקיש's פסוק really does seem to clash with רבי יוחנן's rule from step 17. The גמרא raises this itself in step 20, and step 21 settles it: one rule is for an adult, the other for a child.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Rabbi Meir found a verse and explained it:
"Incline your ear and hear the words of the wise,
phrases.notes: משלי 22:17

phrases.english: and apply your heart to My knowledge";
it does not say "to their knowledge" but "to My knowledge."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: רַבִּי מֵאִיר קְרָא אַשְׁכַּח וּדְרַשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how רבי מאיר could learn from אחר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a different פסוק that supports רבי מאיר's way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: You may never learn from a teacher who is not like an angel.
steps.terutzMaskana: You may listen to a flawed teacher if you hold on only to ה׳'s truth in what he teaches.

steps.title: רב חנינא: a second פסוק from תהלים
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא brings another פסוק: listen and incline your ear, but forget your people and your father's house, meaning drop the bad parts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא said it comes from here: 'Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear, and forget your people and your father's house.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא gives a different source for the same idea, that רבי מאיר could learn from אחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק says to listen carefully and also to 'forget' certain things. Here that means you take the good תורה and forget the teacher's bad ways. It reaches the same answer as ריש לקיש from a different פסוק.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ריש לקיש and רב חנינא explain רבי מאיר the same way: listen to the תורה, and leave behind the teacher's bad ways.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina said it comes from here:
"Listen, daughter, and see, and incline your ear,
phrases.notes: תהלים 45:11

phrases.english: and forget your people and your father's house, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different פסוק for the same answer ריש לקיש gave.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second פסוק supporting the same idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning from a flawed teacher is never allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Listen to the תורה and forget the bad parts of the teacher.

steps.title: The verses seem to contradict each other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the פסוק of רבי יוחנן (learn only from a teacher like an angel) clashes with the פסוקים of ריש לקיש and רב חנינא (you may learn from a flawed teacher).
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses contradict each other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the פסוקים quoted so far point in opposite directions. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's פסוק says you may only learn from a teacher who is like a מלאך. The פסוקים in steps 18-19 allow learning from a flawed teacher if you take only the good. Both cannot be true without some distinction.

phrases.english: The verses contradict each other?
phrases.notes: He means the angel-teacher פסוק from step 17 against the פסוקים in steps 18 and 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the answers of steps 18-19 against the original source in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The פסוקים of steps 18-19 compared with רבי יוחנן's פסוק in step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק forbids learning from an unworthy teacher and the others allow it, so they seem to contradict.

steps.title: Adult versus child
steps.stepSummary: No contradiction: an adult may learn from a flawed teacher, while a child must learn only from a righteous one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This verse is about an adult, and that verse is about a child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each פסוק is about a different kind of student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mature adult can sort the good from the bad, so he may learn from a flawed teacher. A child may copy the teacher's bad ways, so he needs a teacher who is like a מלאך. That is how רבי מאיר, an adult גדול, could learn from אחר.
steps.whatToRemember: An adult may learn from a flawed teacher by taking only the good. A child should learn only from a righteous teacher.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the practical rule behind the whole רבי מאיר and אחר discussion: who may learn from whom depends on the student's maturity.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this is about an adult,
that is about a minor.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּגָדוֹל, הָא בְּקָטָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוקים argue about whether anyone may learn from a flawed teacher.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission applies to an adult and the restriction applies to a child.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: רבי מאיר ate the date and threw the peel away
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports a saying from ארץ ישראל: רבי מאיר ate the fruit and threw away the peel, meaning he took the good תורה from אחר and dropped the bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said: In the West they say, רבי מאיר ate a half-ripe date and threw the peel outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a popular saying that backs up רבי מאיר's choice to learn from אחר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture matches the answer of the last steps. The 'date' is אחר's תורה, which רבי מאיר kept. The 'peel' is אחר's bad ways, which he threw away.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said,
they say in the West:
Rabbi Meir ate a half-ripe date,
and threw the peel outside.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר, אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a saying that supports the conclusion that רבי מאיר took only the good.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר kept אחר's תורה and threw away his bad ways.

steps.title: Torah scholars are like nuts
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains a פסוק in שיר השירים: like a nut whose inside stays clean even when the shell is dirty, a scholar's תורה is not ruined by his sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא taught: What does the פסוק mean, 'I went down to the garden of nuts, to look at the green plants of the valley'? Why are תלמידי חכמים compared to nuts? To teach you that a nut can be covered in mud and filth, yet what is inside is not made disgusting. So too a תלמיד חכם: even if he sinned, his תורה is not made disgusting.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a דרשה with another picture showing that a sinning scholar's תורה keeps its value.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The shell is the person's behavior and the nut inside is his תורה. Dirt on the outside does not reach the inside. That is why the תורה of someone like אחר can still be learned.

phrases.english: Rava taught: What is that which is written:
"I went down into the garden of nuts,
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 6:11

phrases.english: to look at the green plants of the valley, etc."
Why are Torah scholars compared to a nut?
To tell you:
Just as this nut,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁמְּלוּכְלָךְ בְּטִיט וּבְצוֹאָה —
phrases.english: even though it is soiled with mud and filth,
what is inside it is not made disgusting;

phrases.aramaic: אַף תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁסָּרַח —
phrases.english: so too a Torah scholar, even though he has sinned,
his Torah is not made disgusting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק-based picture of the same idea as the date-and-peel saying.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A scholar's sins do not spoil the value of his תורה.

steps.title: רבה בר שילא asks אליהו what ה׳ is doing
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא meets אליהו and asks him what הקדוש ברוך הוא is busy with.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שילא met אליהו. He asked him: What is הקדוש ברוך הוא doing?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. The opening question sets up אליהו's report about רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question lets us see how Heaven itself looks at רבי מאיר learning from אחר. The answer shows the issue is not only a human debate.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Sheila found Elijah.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי קָא עָבֵיד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to him: What is the Holy One, Blessed be He, doing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a story that tests the idea that learning from אחר was acceptable.

steps.title: ה׳ quotes every sage except רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that ה׳ is saying הלכות in the names of all the sages, but not in the name of רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He is saying teachings from the mouths of all the Rabbis, but from the mouth of רבי מאיר He is not saying anything.
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו answers the question and reveals that רבי מאיר is being left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is surprising, since רבי מאיר was one of the greatest תנאים. It creates the puzzle that the next steps explain.

phrases.english: He said to him: He is saying teachings
from the mouths of all the Rabbis,
but from the mouth of Rabbi Meir He does not say.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ה׳ says הלכות from all the sages except רבי מאיר.

steps.title: Why? Because he learned from אחר
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא asks why, and אליהו explains it is because רבי מאיר learned from אחר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He asked him: Why? Because he learned teachings from the mouth of אחר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא asks for the reason, and אליהו gives it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This brings back the original problem from step 17 at a heavenly level. Learning from a teacher who turned bad seems to cost רבי מאיר his place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the other one', the name for אלישע בן אבויה after he left the right path

phrases.english: He said to him: Why?
Because he learned teachings
from the mouth of Aḥer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי? מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא גָמַר שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבי מאיר was left out in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because רבי מאיר learned from אחר.

steps.title: But רבי מאיר ate the pomegranate and threw away the peel
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שילא objects: why punish רבי מאיר? He found a pomegranate, ate the inside, and threw away the peel.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why? רבי מאיר found a pomegranate. He ate the inside and threw away the peel.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר שילא challenges the heavenly reason and defends רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses the same idea as the date and the nut. רבי מאיר kept only the good תורה, so learning from אחר should not count against him.

phrases.english: He said to him: Why?
phrases.notes: This time רבה בר שילא is protesting: why should רבי מאיר be held back for this?

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir found a pomegranate,
he ate its inside and threw away its peel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לֵיהּ: אַמַּאי? רַבִּי מֵאִיר רִמּוֹן מָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The heavenly reason for not quoting רבי מאיר (step 26)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר kept only the good part of אחר's תורה, as step 21 allows for an adult, so he should not be held back.

steps.title: ה׳ now quotes 'Meir My son'
steps.stepSummary: אליהו says that after this defense ה׳ is now quoting רבי מאיר: when a person suffers, the שכינה cries out in pain, and so all the more for the spilled blood of צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Now He is saying: 'My son מאיר says: When a person suffers, what does the שכינה say? "I am in pain from My head, I am in pain from My arm." If הקדוש ברוך הוא suffers this much over the blood of the wicked, it is a קל וחומר that He suffers over the spilled blood of the righteous.'
steps.whatsHappening: The defense works. ה׳ quotes רבי מאיר again, calling him 'My son', and we hear the teaching He quotes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heaven accepts that רבי מאיר acted rightly, which confirms the answer of step 21. The teaching itself says ה׳ feels pain even when wicked people are punished, so He surely feels pain for צדיקים who suffer.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I am lightened', a gentle way of saying 'woe is Me'
an argument from a lighter case to a stronger one

steps.whatToRemember: Heaven itself approved of רבי מאיר learning from אחר, because he took the inside and threw away the peel.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now He is saying,
My son Meir says:
When a person suffers,
what words does the Divine Presence say?
Woe is Me from My head, woe is Me from My arm.
phrases.notes: Literally 'I am light'. It is a softened way of saying that ה׳ feels the pain Himself.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כָּךְ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִצְטַעֵר
phrases.english: If the Holy One, Blessed be He, suffers so much
over the blood of the wicked,

phrases.aramaic: קַל וָחוֹמֶר עַל דָּמָן שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים שֶׁנִּשְׁפַּךְ.
phrases.english: all the more so over the blood of the righteous that is spilled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא קָאָמַר, מֵאִיר בְּנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows Heaven accepting the defense raised in step 27.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי מאיר is quoted again in Heaven, which proves his learning from אחר was proper.

steps.title: שמואל finds רב יהודה crying
steps.stepSummary: שמואל finds his student רב יהודה leaning on the door bar and crying, and asks him why.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל found רב יהודה leaning on the bar of the door and crying. He said to him: Sharp one! Why are you crying?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins with a question that sets up רב יהודה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story moves on from רבי מאיר to a related fear: if great scholars can go wrong, who is safe? The answer comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: 'sharp-toothed one', שמואל's nickname for רב יהודה

phrases.english: Shmuel found Rav Yehuda
leaning on the bar of the door and crying.
He said to him: Long-toothed one!
phrases.notes: A fond nickname שמואל used for his sharp student רב יהודה.

phrases.english: Why are you crying?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה דִּתְלֵי בְּעִיבְרָא דְּדַשָּׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story about great scholars who went astray.

steps.title: רב יהודה cites the פסוק about the great scholars
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה answers that what the פסוק says about the sages is no small matter: 'Where is he who counted, where is he who weighed, where is he who counted the towers?'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it a small thing, what is written about the Rabbis: 'Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the towers?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains that he is crying because of a פסוק about great sages.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק asks 'where are they?', as if these great people are gone or lost. That frightens רב יהודה, and the next step explains how great they were.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it a small matter
what is written about the Rabbis:
"Where is he who counted, where is he who weighed,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 33:18

phrases.english: where is he who counted the towers?"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי זוּטְרָא מַאי דִּכְתִיב בְּהוּ בְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's question from step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is crying over the פסוק in ישעיהו about great sages.

steps.title: How great those scholars were
steps.stepSummary: Each part of the פסוק is explained: they counted every letter of the תורה, weighed its light and serious laws, and learned 300 הלכות about a tower floating in the air.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Where is he who counted': they counted all the letters in the תורה. 'Where is he who weighed': they weighed the light and serious matters in the תורה. 'Where is he who counted the towers': they learned three hundred הלכות about a tower floating in the air.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה explains the פסוק piece by piece to show how great these scholars were.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק is tied to a kind of deep תורה learning. The more amazing these scholars were, the scarier it is that they could still go wrong, and that is why רב יהודה cries.

keyTerms.meaning: a tower floating in the air

phrases.english: "Where is he who counted":
for they would count all the letters in the Torah.
"Where is he who weighed":
for they would weigh the light and serious matters in the Torah.
"Where is he who counted the towers":
for they would learn three hundred halakhot
about a tower floating in the air.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״אַיֵּה סוֹפֵר״ — שֶׁהָיוּ סוֹפְרִים כׇּל אוֹתִיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the פסוק quoted in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק describes scholars who mastered every letter, every light and serious law, and even the most unusual הלכות.

steps.title: Great scholars who still lost their share
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי says דואג and אחיתופל asked 300 questions about the floating tower. A משנה says that three kings and four commoners, including them, have no share in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: דואג and אחיתופל asked three hundred questions about a tower floating in the air. And a משנה teaches: three kings and four commoners have no share in the World to Come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how great דואג and אחיתופל were in Torah, and then reminds us that they still lost their share in עולם הבא. This sets up רב יהודה's fear in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part shows they were giants in hard Torah questions, like the 300 laws mentioned in Step 31. The משנה shows that this greatness did not save them. Put together, these two facts create the scary question that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Two great scholars in the time of דוד המלך who sinned badly
Commoners, people who were not kings
A share in the World to Come

phrases.english: And Rabbi Ami said:
Three hundred questions
Doeg and Achitophel asked
about a tower floating in the air.
And we learned in a Mishnah:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in סנהדרין 90a.

phrases.english: Three kings and four commoners
have no share in the World to Come.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: תְּלָת מְאָה בַּעְיֵי בְּעוֹ דּוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתוֹפֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to the 'floating tower' idea from Step 31 and brings a משנה that builds up רב יהודה's worry.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even scholars as great as דואג and אחיתופל lost their share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: What hope is there for us?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's fear: if such great scholars were lost, what will happen to us?
steps.simpleTranslation: We, what will become of us?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of why רב יהודה was crying. If giants like דואג and אחיתופל fell, people like us have even less protection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is a kind of reasoning from big to small: Torah greatness did not protect them, so it surely won't protect us. This is a real, painful question, and שמואל will answer it next.

phrases.english: We, what will become of us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the painful conclusion from Step 32: if they fell, we are in danger.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can ordinary scholars hope to be saved if great scholars were lost?

steps.title: שמואל: they had mud in their hearts
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that דואג and אחיתופל had a flaw in their hearts. Their Torah was not the problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Sharp one! There was mud in their hearts.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל calms רב יהודה. Those scholars fell because their hearts were not clean, not because Torah fails to protect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'mud' is a hidden inner flaw that was there from the start. So their fall does not prove anything about a person with a pure heart. This idea will be shown with אחר and with רבי מאיר's wool picture.

keyTerms.meaning: A nickname שמואל used for רב יהודה, meaning 'sharp one' or 'long-toothed one'

steps.whatToRemember: Torah protects a person whose heart is clean. People who fell despite great learning had a flaw inside from the start.

phrases.english: He said to him: Sharp one!
There was mud in their hearts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שִׁינָּנָא! טִינָא הָיְתָה בְּלִבָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יהודה's fear from Step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Their fall came from a flaw in their hearts, so it is no threat to scholars whose hearts are pure.

steps.title: What was אחר's flaw? Greek songs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what was wrong with אחר, and answers that Greek songs never left his mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Acher, what was his flaw? Greek song never stopped coming from his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses שמואל's idea for אחר too. It shows that he also had a hidden flaw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחר was a great scholar who went wrong after entering the פרדס. The גמרא shows he was always drawn to Greek culture, even while among the sages. So his fall fits the 'mud in the heart' idea.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The other one,' the name used for אלישע בן אבויה after he left the right path

steps.confusionAlert: אחר is not a different person from the story of the four who entered the פרדס. It is the nickname for אלישע בן אבויה.

phrases.english: Acher, what was his flaw?
Greek song never stopped from his mouth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחֵר מַאי — זֶמֶר יְווֹנִי לָא פְּסַק מִפּוּמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses שמואל's answer from Step 34 for the case of אחר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: אחר's flaw was his love of Greek song, which showed a pull toward non-Jewish culture.

steps.title: Heretical books fell from אחר's lap
steps.stepSummary: Another report about אחר: when he stood up in the בית המדרש, heretical books would fall from his lap.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said about Acher: when he would stand up in the study hall, many heretical books would fall from his lap.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings more support that אחר had a flaw from the start. Even in the בית המדרש he carried heretical books.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a second sign to the Greek songs. It shows that his heart was already split while he was learning Torah. So his fall does not show that Torah failed him.

phrases.english: They said about Acher:
When he would stand up in the study hall,
many heretical books
would fall from his lap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof of אחר's flaw.
steps.raayaObject: That אחר had a flaw in his heart from the start
steps.raayaSupportSource: The report that heretical books fell from his lap in the בית המדרש

steps.title: Does all wool come out dyed?
steps.stepSummary: נימוס הגרדי asks רבי מאיר whether all wool put in the dye pot comes out colored.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nimos the weaver asked רבי מאיר: does all wool that goes down into the dye pot come out colored?
steps.whatsHappening: A non-Jewish thinker asks רבי מאיר a question using a picture. He is really asking whether everyone who learns Torah comes out good.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dye pot stands for Torah, and the wool stands for the learner. The question fits our topic: why did some great learners, like אחר, not come out good?

keyTerms.meaning: Nimos the weaver, a non-Jewish philosopher
A large pot, here a dye pot
Comes up, comes out well (here: comes out dyed)

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל נִימוֹס הַגַּרְדִּי אֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Nimos the weaver asked Rabbi Meir:
Does all wool that goes down into the dye pot come out colored?
phrases.notes: He is really asking about people: does everyone who learns Torah come out good?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל נִימוֹס הַגַּרְדִּי אֶת רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parable that fits the idea that a learner's inner condition decides the result.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does Torah learning make every learner good?

steps.title: Only wool that was clean from the start
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers: wool that was clean while still on its mother comes out dyed. Wool that was not clean does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: whatever was clean while on its mother comes out dyed; whatever was not clean while on its mother does not come out dyed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר answers that it depends on how the wool started out. In the same way, Torah works well only on a person who came to it clean.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wool that was dirty on the sheep will not take the dye. A person with a flaw from the start, like אחר, will not be properly shaped by Torah. This backs up שמואל's 'mud in the heart' answer.

keyTerms.meaning: While on its mother (the sheep), meaning from the very start

steps.whatToRemember: Torah 'colors' a person only if he comes to it clean. A flaw from the start can stop Torah from changing him.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל מַאן דַּהֲוָה נְקֵי אַגַּב אִימֵּיהּ — סָלֵיק,
phrases.english: Whatever was clean while on its mother comes out dyed,
phrases.notes: 'On its mother' means while the wool was still on the sheep, before it was cut.

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל דְּלָא הֲוָה נְקֵי אַגַּב אִימֵּיהּ — לָא סָלֵיק.
phrases.english: whatever was not clean while on its mother does not come out dyed.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּל מַאן דַּהֲוָה נְקֵי אַגַּב אִימֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers נימוס's question from Step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only a learner who was pure from the start is truly changed by Torah.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא went up and came down in peace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the four in the פרדס: רבי עקיבא went up and came down safely, and a פסוק is applied to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went up in peace and came down in peace, and about him the verse says: 'Draw me, we will run after You.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of the four who entered the פרדס. It now explains the line about רבי עקיבא, the only one who came out safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After explaining why others fell, the גמרא shows the opposite: רבי עקיבא was clean, so he was safe. The פסוק shows that ה׳ drew him close, and he followed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Draw me, we will run after You'

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva went up in peace
and came down in peace,
and about him the verse says:
'Draw me, we will run after You.'
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 1:4

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עָלָה בְּשָׁלוֹם וְיָרַד בְּשָׁלוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about flawed scholars and returns to the story of the four in the פרדס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא went up and came down safely, as the פסוק 'Draw me, we will run after You' describes.

steps.title: ה׳ protects רבי עקיבא from the angels
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי עקיבא was almost pushed out by the angels, but ה׳ told them to leave him because he was worthy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even רבי עקיבא, the ministering angels wanted to push him away. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them: Leave this elder alone, for he is worthy to make use of My glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that רבי עקיבא's safety was not automatic. The angels wanted to push him out, but ה׳ Himself protected him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows how dangerous the פרדס was, even for the greatest. רבי עקיבא came out safely because ה׳ said he was worthy. This matches the פסוק in the last step, where ה׳ 'draws' him in.

keyTerms.meaning: To make use of My glory

steps.whatToRemember: Of the four who entered the פרדס, only רבי עקיבא came out safely, and even he was saved only because ה׳ said he was worthy.

phrases.english: And even Rabbi Akiva,
the ministering angels wanted to push him away,
The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to them:
Leave this elder alone,
for he is worthy to make use of My glory.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בִּקְּשׁוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לְדוֹחְפוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to Step 39 about how רבי עקיבא came out safely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא was saved from the angels because ה׳ said he was worthy.
